Let me take you through the page. The default rate is four point two per cent this quarter, against a baseline of three point one, so we are one point one above where we started and zero point two above target. Roughly a third of the base is now in the pilot, and the sample is finally big enough to trust. Two months ago it was not, and I said so at the time. The average limit is eight hundred reais. I am going to say that number once, and then I am going to ask you to forget it, because hardly any customer sits at eight hundred. The range goes from three hundred to five thousand, and the range is where the story is. Revenue exceeded the target by eleven per cent, and most of the losses come from the customers who joined in April.

In the nineteen forties the American air force had a problem with crashes, and for a while they blamed the pilots. Then somebody measured four thousand of them: height, arm length, chest, ten measurements in all. The cockpit was designed for the average pilot, so the question was simple. How many of the four thousand were average on all ten? The answer was none. Not a small number. None. And on just three of the ten, fewer than four in a hundred. That is what an average always does. It hides the range, and the two ends of the range are where the interesting cases live. So whenever somebody shows you an average, ask two things. How many people are actually near it, and what do the two ends look like? If nobody can answer, the number is decoration.
